items.title: California DP-1 Declaration of Domestic Partnership
items.notes: Use the regular/public DP-1 unless counsel gives a reason to use the confidential filing. Both partners sign the same original; signatures may be notarized separately abroad.

items.title: Notarize both DP-1 signatures
items.notes: Use an acceptable notary route in Japan/US. Keep the original document intact for filing.

items.title: File DP-1 with California Secretary of State
items.notes: File the original and pay the current state fee. Courier/in-person processing can be used if desired.
items.caution: Fees and processing options can change; verify before submission.

items.title: Obtain certified copy of filed domestic partnership
items.notes: Use the certified file-stamped declaration as the primary relationship record for Spain.
items.caution: Do not rely only on a decorative/commemorative certificate.

items.title: California apostille for certified partnership record
items.notes: Apostille the California-issued certified record, then send the entire apostilled packet for sworn Spanish translation.

items.title: Complete passport scans for Irving
items.notes: Scan every page; after Spain entry include the entry stamp/entry evidence.

items.title: NIE documentation
items.notes: Keep the NIE certificate/record available for filings and banking.

items.title: Current employment contract
items.notes: Use the complete signed current agreement showing the employment relationship.
items.caution: Confirm whether counsel wants the full agreement translated.

items.title: Fresh Spain-specific posted-worker / remote-work employer letter
items.notes: State role, detailed duties, salary, start date, 100% remote work, explicit authorization to work from Spain, assignment duration, and posted-worker rationale.
items.caution: This is a core W-2 risk item; wording should be reviewed by the immigration lawyer.

items.title: SSA Certificate of Coverage
items.notes: Employer requests the certificate under the U.S.-Spain social-security agreement and the application is structured as a temporary posting to Spain.
items.caution: Potentially one of the slowest documents; start early.

items.title: Delaware Certificate of Good Standing / Status
items.notes: Shows the foreign company has existed/operated for at least one year.
items.caution: Use a state-issued record suitable for apostille; do not substitute a simple notarized copy.

items.title: Supporting proof of employer real/continuous activity
items.notes: Keep company website, payroll/business records and other activity evidence available in case UGE requests more proof.

items.title: FBI Identity History Summary
items.notes: Order late enough to stay fresh but early enough to complete the federal apostille.

items.title: Other police certificates based on residence history
items.notes: Have counsel map the prior two years of actual residence. Japan is likely relevant; Thailand should be confirmed based on status and residence history.
items.caution: Do not order unnecessary country certificates until residence history is confirmed.

items.title: Responsible declaration of no criminal record for prior 5 years
items.notes: Separate declaration from official police certificates.

items.title: Professional experience letters covering 3+ years
items.notes: Use employer letters with dates, titles and detailed software-engineering duties.

items.title: Government evidence matching professional experience
items.notes: Prepare W-2s, IRS transcripts/tax records and/or SSA earnings evidence that match the employer experience letters.
items.caution: Counsel should choose the cleanest set before apostilles/translations.

items.title: One-page CV / resume
items.notes: Recent experience with clear software-engineering chronology.

items.title: Three most recent pay stubs
items.notes: Make sure gross salary and payroll dates line up with bank deposits.

items.title: Three months of stamped/signed bank statements
items.notes: Use statements showing payroll deposits. Highlight only relevant deposits and prepare a trace sheet.
items.caution: Confirm bank certification/signature requirements close to filing.

items.title: Spain-compliant private health insurance
items.notes: Policy for Irving and Moeno: Spain-authorized insurer, no copay, no deductible, full coverage, and prepaid if counsel requires.
items.caution: Employee/CoC health treatment is separate from social-security coordination; follow counsel's current requirement.

items.title: Sworn Spanish translations of final apostilled documents
items.notes: Translate only final versions after apostilles/legalizations are complete.

items.title: Proof of lawful entry / presence in Spain
items.notes: Prefer entering Schengen directly through Spain. Preserve boarding passes and entry evidence; obtain an entry declaration if counsel instructs.

items.title: Submit DNV from inside Spain
items.notes: Lawyer files electronically while Irving is lawfully present in Spain; submit Moeno simultaneously as family member when packet is ready.

items.title: Complete passport scan for Moeno
items.notes: All passport pages; add Spain/Schengen entry evidence if filing in Spain.

items.title: California domestic partnership certificate + apostille + sworn translation
items.notes: Primary relationship evidence for Moeno's family-member application.
items.caution: Keep backup relationship evidence available even though registration is the primary route.

items.title: Moeno criminal-record certificate(s)
items.notes: Japanese police certificate and any other certificate counsel determines is required from residence history.

items.title: Moeno 5-year no-criminal-record declaration
items.notes: Adult family-member declaration.

items.title: Moeno health coverage
items.notes: Include Moeno on compliant private health coverage if not otherwise entitled.

items.title: Financial means for Irving + Moeno
items.notes: Salary is expected to be comfortably above threshold; still prove it using current official formula and recent income evidence.
items.caution: Do not hard-code old income figures; recalculate at filing.

items.title: Simultaneous family-member application reference
items.notes: Link Moeno's application to Irving's teleworker filing/authorization.

items.title: Secure Spain housing that permits padrón and dog
items.notes: Prefer both names on lease where possible. Confirm padrón permission and Mui acceptance.

items.title: Register both partners on padrón
items.notes: Keep historical padrón records for future citizenship evidence.

items.title: Book TIE fingerprint appointments
items.notes: Book as soon as favorable resolutions arrive.

items.title: Prepare TIE appointment packet
items.notes: Passports, favorable resolutions, forms, photos, fee proof and padrón if required by the police station.

items.title: Collect TIE cards
items.notes: Keep copies of both cards and track expiry.

items.title: Keep Spanish bank account active / update address
items.notes: N26 already opened; update residency/address data when appropriate.

items.title: Hire Spain/U.S. cross-border tax adviser
items.notes: Adviser should understand U.S. citizens, Spain DNV, treaty, foreign tax credits/FEIE interactions, New York domicile questions and Spanish special regimes.

items.title: Maintain U.S. social-security coverage under CoC structure
items.notes: Do not register as autónomo if approved as a W-2 employee under the Certificate of Coverage route unless counsel changes the structure.

items.title: Evaluate/apply for Spanish impatriate (Beckham) regime
items.notes: Get tax counsel to determine eligibility and deadline under the exact employee/posted-worker facts.
items.caution: Missing a tax election deadline can be irreversible.

items.title: Employer Spanish payroll / permanent-establishment review
items.notes: Company should document that Irving does not sign contracts, manage Spanish market activity, or otherwise create unnecessary Spanish presence.
items.caution: Tax counsel should assess the employer's actual facts; do not assume zero risk.

items.title: Verify Mui microchip and rabies sequencing
items.notes: Confirm ISO-compatible microchip and rabies vaccination dates/validity.

items.title: Reserve Iberia pet transport and compliant crate
items.notes: Confirm route, weight, crate dimensions and advance reservation requirements.

items.title: Japan AQS export process
items.notes: Apply for export inspection and prepare required animal-health documents.

items.title: EU animal health certificate / non-commercial movement declaration
items.notes: Coordinate timing with veterinarian and Japan export inspection.

items.title: Obtain EU pet passport in Spain
items.notes: Useful for later EU travel.

items.title: Build proof that Dominican nationality is nationality of origin
items.notes: Keep Dominican passport, cédula, nationality/registration documents and parentage evidence. Have nationality counsel confirm the two-year rule applies to Irving's facts.
items.caution: Important because Irving was born in the U.S.; document the legal basis before relying on the accelerated period.

items.title: Maintain complete Spain absence/travel log
items.notes: Track every exit/entry, boarding pass and passport stamp. Avoid long/repetitive absences that could jeopardize continuity.

items.title: Maintain continuous-residence evidence
items.notes: Keep padrón history, leases, bank activity, tax filings, TIEs and employment evidence.

items.title: Prepare and pass CCSE
items.notes: Take early enough that the certificate is available before nationality filing.

items.title: Confirm DELE A2 exemption
items.notes: Confirm exemption based on Dominican nationality with nationality counsel/Instituto Cervantes rules rather than assuming.

items.title: Citizenship-file audit with nationality lawyer
items.notes: Audit continuity, absences, Dominican origin evidence, civil-status docs, police records and exam/exemption status.

items.title: File Spanish nationality application when eligible
items.leadTime: ~24 months after qualifying legal residence begins
items.notes: File only after counsel confirms two years of legal and continuous qualifying residence are complete.

items.title: Current New York driver licence
items.notes: Original plus copy.

items.title: NY licence certification / lifetime driving record
items.notes: Complete the New York authentication/apostille chain required for use abroad.

items.title: Dominican passport and cédula
items.notes: Bring originals and copies.

items.title: Confirm INTRANT conversion eligibility for Dominican citizen
items.notes: Confirm whether Dominican cédula is sufficient and exactly which U.S. licence certification is accepted.

items.title: Obtain written DGT confirmation before relying on DR→Spain exchange
items.leadTime: Before pursuing DR licence as Spain strategy
items.notes: Spain can exclude licences that were themselves obtained by exchange from a non-agreement country.
items.caution: High-risk strategy; do not rely on it without written DGT confirmation.
